question.worked_solution:
First, we let

$$
I=\int \frac{{ln}^{2}⁡x}{4x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

To use integration by parts, let's suppose that

$$
\begin{aligned}u={ln}^{2}⁡x & \,⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{4x} & \,⇒\,v=\int \frac{1}{4x}\text{d}x=\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{4}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\int \frac{{ln}^{2}⁡x}{4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={ln}^{2}⁡x(\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{4})-\int (\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{4})(\frac{2\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{ln}^{3}⁡x}{4}-2\int \frac{{ln}^{2}⁡x}{4x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{ln}^{3}⁡x}{4}-2I.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $I,$ remembering to add a constant of integration $C$ at the very end:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\frac{{ln}^{3}⁡x}{4}-2I \\ 3I & =\frac{{ln}^{3}⁡x}{4} \\ I & =\frac{{ln}^{3}⁡x}{12}+C\end{aligned}
$$
